feedback: Written before this candidate races, so no outcome is claimed for it. The evidence is iteration 0 (score 49.8, 0 of 60 trials finished). Every trial went off track at progress 0.10 to 0.15, with max_error about 0.06 m and one line-loss event each. That pattern points to the robot losing the line early, not drifting slowly. The candidate is valid: all values are inside their contract limits, and its sign convention is correct (negative x weights steer right, positive signal steers left). The changes are coherent with the baseline failure: base_speed drops from 1.6 to 1.4, kd rises from 0.1 to 0.4 for damping, sensor look-ahead moves from y 0.04 to 0.03 to cut reaction lag, and mass falls to 0.6 kg. One risk is that kp rises from 2.0 to 3.0 at the same time. That raises the maximum turn command by 50%, and with base_speed still at 1.4 it could cause oscillation on the slalom. Body width cannot help the off-track limit much: at body_width 0.18 the limit is about 0.0575 m, which is still below the current 0.06 m. This is early exploration with 10 iterations left and no raced build yet, so the bar is validity and not obvious breakage. The candidate meets that bar, and only a race will show whether the combined change works. Approve it so the race produces per-track telemetry. After the race, use the numbers to decide the next step. If line_loss_events is still 1 or more with max_error near 0.06 on the s-bend, the cause is turn overshoot: raise kd further before anything else. If progress stalls on the slalom or steering_oscillation is high, kp is too high: bring it back toward 2.0 and keep kd at 0.4. If the run completes cleanly with low rms_error, raise base_speed in steps of 0.2 to find the limit.
requested_changes: If the race shows max_error near 0.06 m or line_loss_events of 1 or more on the s-bend, keep kp at 3.0 and raise kd from 0.4 toward 0.6 to damp turn overshoot, because the baseline failed on all three tracks at the same early point.

If the race shows high steering_oscillation or progress stalling on the slalom, reduce kp from 3.0 toward 2.0 while keeping kd at 0.4, because the candidate raised kp by 50% at the same time as base_speed fell.

If the race completes with low max_error and rms_error and completion_time well under 3 s, raise base_speed from 1.4 toward 1.6 in steps of 0.2 with the same gains, to find the speed limit before tracking fails.
